text: Jaipur is Rajasthan's capital and one point of the Delhi-Agra-Jaipur Golden Triangle. It was established in 1727 by Jai Singh II and is known as the Pink City.
Jaipur's listed highlights include City Palace, Hawa Mahal and Amber Fort. The official destination page also describes Jaipur's historic pink-painted cityscape.
Jaipur is served by Jaipur International Airport (JAI) and Jaipur Junction Railway Station (JP), as listed by Incredible India.
The Incredible India Jaipur guide recommends dal bati churma, kachoris and ghevar as local foods to try.
General India travel guidance: respect local dress codes and customs, particularly at religious sites and in rural areas.
General India travel guidance warns that scammers, pickpockets and ticket touts target visitors in tourist areas. Check sellers and ticket agents before paying.
General India travel advice recommends following local authority guidance, keeping belongings secure on public transport and in crowds, and using emergency number 112 when needed.
Udaipur, known as the City of Lakes, is set among the Aravalli hills and is noted for its lakes, palaces and Rajput heritage. Maharana Udai Singh II founded the city in 1553.
Udaipur highlights include Lake Pichola, the City Palace complex and Jag Mandir Palace on an island in Lake Pichola.
Udaipur is served by Maharana Pratap Airport (UDR) and Udaipur City Railway Station (UDZ), according to the Incredible India destination guide.

Jodhpur, also called the Blue City and Sun City, was founded in 1459 by Rao Jodha and served as the capital of the former Marwar kingdom.
Jodhpur highlights include Mehrangarh Fort, Umaid Bhawan Palace, Jaswant Thada and the old city's blue-painted buildings.
Jodhpur is served by Jodhpur Airport and Jodhpur Railway Station, as listed in the Incredible India travel information.

Jaisalmer, the Golden City, lies in the Thar Desert and has historic havelis, bazaars and desert landscapes. Its fort is described as a living fort, with residents, temples, shops and restaurants inside its walls.
Jaisalmer's destination guide highlights Jaisalmer Fort, Patwon Ki Haveli, Kuldhara, Akal Wood Fossil Park and Gadisar Lake.
The Incredible India travel listing names Jaisalmer Airport (JSR), Jodhpur Airport (JFR) and Jaisalmer Railway Station (JSM) for access to Jaisalmer.
Incredible India recommends November to March for visiting Jaisalmer, when its guide describes temperatures as mild and outdoor excursions as being at their peak.
Jaisalmer's guide names mirchi bhajiya, pyaz ki kachori, dal baati churma, gatte ki sabzi, kadhi, ker sangri and laal maas among local foods.
